'''Jason Bermas''' (born July 24, 1980) is an American filmmaker and conspiracy theorist known for his involvement in the creation of the documentary ''Loose Change''. The film is one of the most prominent works in the 9/11 Truth movement, presenting alternative theories about the September 11 attacks. Bermas has been associated with several controversial projects and has become a notable figure in conspiracy circles.

==Career==
In the mid-2000s, Bermas co-produced ''Loose Change'' alongside Dylan Avery and Korey Rowe. The documentary posits that the official narrative provided by the U.S. government regarding the events of September 11, 2001, is incomplete, suggesting instead that they might have been an inside job. The film gained significant attention and was both widely criticized and praised within different circles.

==Controversies==
Bermas has been involved in numerous controversies due to his promotion of conspiracy theories. He has been accused of spreading misinformation and fostering distrust in official institutions. His work has often been criticized by experts and skeptics who argue that it lacks credible evidence and substantial fact-checking.

==Connection with Alex Jones==
Bermas has been linked with [[Alex Jones]], a prominent conspiracy theorist and founder of [[InfoWars]]. He has appeared on several of Jones's broadcasts, discussing various conspiracy theories and promoting alternative narratives regarding political and historical events. The association with Jones has further fueled criticisms of Bermas as promoting unfounded and sensationalist information.

==Public Perception==
Public perception of Jason Bermas is polarized. While some view him as a whistleblower challenging mainstream narratives, others see him as a purveyor of conspiracy theories that can have harmful societal impacts. Despite criticism, Bermas continues to be active in the conspiracy theory community, leveraging various online platforms to reach a broader audience.
